overview.title: What Is a CDN?
overview.p1: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) is a network of edge servers distributed across multiple regions. When a user visits your site, the CDN routes the request to the node physically closest to them instead of forcing every request back to a single origin server, shortening the data path, reducing latency, and easing the load on your origin infrastructure.
overview.p2: Kineticlinks operates over 100 edge nodes across Asia-Pacific, North America, and Europe, using intelligent routing to continuously measure latency and congestion at each node and automatically select the fastest path. Whether your users are in Taiwan, mainland China, Southeast Asia, or Western markets, they get access speeds close to a local server.
overview.p3: Beyond acceleration, a CDN is also your first line of defense against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Kineticlinks provides terabit-scale scrubbing capacity that filters malicious traffic at the edge before it ever reaches your origin server, keeping your business running without interruption.

overview.p3: To minimize data loss risk, every VPS instance includes scheduled automatic backups and snapshots, preserving multiple recovery points so you can restore quickly after an incident — letting your team focus on building the product instead of routine infrastructure upkeep.

overview.title: What Is an SSL Certificate Automation Platform?
overview.p1: An SSL certificate is required to enable HTTPS on a website, but the traditional request, validation, and renewal process is often manual: creating DNS validation records by hand, downloading certificate files, and uploading them one by one to servers or CDNs. overview.p2: The Kineticlinks SSL automation platform ties the whole process into a single interface. Once a certificate is issued, it can also be pushed automatically to multiple CDN brands, connecting certificate deployment directly to your CDN acceleration setup.
overview.p3: The platform also provides expiration reminders and automatic renewal, reducing the risk of a certificate lapsing due to human oversight — especially useful for teams managing many domains or frequently switching certificates between CDN providers.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Are there limits on the free speed test?
faq.a1: The free tier offers real-time web-based testing, suited for individual, infrequent checks. If you need scheduled automated tests or high query volume, consider the commercial API plan.
faq.q2: Can the commercial API integrate with our own monitoring system?
faq.a2: Yes. The commercial API is designed to plug directly into your existing monitoring dashboard or alerting system, making it easy to track connection quality trends for specific nodes over time.
faq.q3: Does testing only cover China's three carriers?
faq.a3: The platform's core focus is China's Telecom, Unicom, and Mobile networks, but it also covers connection quality testing across other major Asia-Pacific markets — it isn't limited to China.
faq.q4: Can I test a specific server or domain?
faq.a4: Yes. You can enter the server address or domain you want to test and get real measured connection data against all three major carriers.
faq.q5: How often is the test data updated?
faq.a5: Results are measured in real time — every test returns the current actual connection status. Scheduled calls through the API let you set your own testing frequency.
